findings.body: The variable name and downstream usage (`!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee`) imply team admins should be authorized, but requiring both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true means only owners (a subset already covered by isTeamAdmin's OR-role query) ever pass, so legitimate team admins are incorrectly forbidden from adding guests (FORBIDDEN error).
findings.failure_mode: Overly restrictive authorization silently blocks a valid user role from performing the action.
findings.impact: The variable name and downstream usage (`!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee`) imply team admins should be authorized, but requiring both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true means only owners (a subset already covered by isTeamAdmin's OR-role query) ever pass, so legitimate team admins are incorrectly forbidden from adding guests (FORBIDDEN error).
findings.root_cause: Boolean operator `&&` was used instead of `||` when combining two role checks that the variable name and downstream conditional treat as an OR relationship.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the `&&` to `||` so a user who is either a team admin or a team owner is authorized: `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) || (await isTeamOwner(...))`.
findings.title: Team admin/owner permission check uses AND instead of OR
findings.trigger: A team ADMIN (not OWNER) who is not the booking organizer or an attendee attempts to add guests to a team booking.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 46-48 show `isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses `&&` between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner. Context shows isTeamAdmin already returns true for ADMIN or OWNER roles (line 270 OR condition). Using && means only users who are both admin AND owner pass, but the variable name and usage at line 54 (`!isTeamAdminOrOwner`) implies OR semantics. This is a real logic bug introduced by the patch.

raw_findings.body: The variable name and downstream usage (`!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee`) imply team admins should be authorized, but requiring both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true means only owners (a subset already covered by isTeamAdmin's OR-role query) ever pass, so legitimate team admins are incorrectly forbidden from adding guests (FORBIDDEN error).
raw_findings.failure_mode: Overly restrictive authorization silently blocks a valid user role from performing the action.
raw_findings.impact: The variable name and downstream usage (`!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee`) imply team admins should be authorized, but requiring both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true means only owners (a subset already covered by isTeamAdmin's OR-role query) ever pass, so legitimate team admins are incorrectly forbidden from adding guests (FORBIDDEN error).
raw_findings.root_cause: Boolean operator `&&` was used instead of `||` when combining two role checks that the variable name and downstream conditional treat as an OR relationship.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Change the `&&` to `||` so a user who is either a team admin or a team owner is authorized: `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) || (await isTeamOwner(...))`.
raw_findings.title: Team admin/owner permission check uses AND instead of OR
raw_findings.trigger: A team ADMIN (not OWNER) who is not the booking organizer or an attendee attempts to add guests to a team booking.

raw_findings.body: Because no `you_do_not_have_permission` key exists in apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json, the toast shown to the user displays the raw untranslated key instead of a human-readable message.
raw_findings.failure_mode: User-facing error message is unreadable/untranslated raw key text.
raw_findings.impact: Because no `you_do_not_have_permission` key exists in apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json, the toast shown to the user displays the raw untranslated key instead of a human-readable message.
raw_findings.root_cause: A new error message key was introduced in code without adding the corresponding locale string.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a `you_do_not_have_permission` entry to apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json (and other locale files) with an appropriate translated message.
raw_findings.title: Missing localization entry for permission-denied error message
raw_findings.trigger: A user without organizer/attendee/team-admin-owner permission calls addGuests, triggering this TRPCError, and the client renders it via `t(err.message)` in AddGuestsDialog.tsx.

raw_findings.body: Both duplicate entries pass the filter (since neither matches an *existing* attendee) and are inserted via createMany, creating duplicate Attendee rows with the same email for the same booking.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Server persists duplicate data despite client-side validation intending to prevent it.
raw_findings.impact: Both duplicate entries pass the filter (since neither matches an *existing* attendee) and are inserted via createMany, creating duplicate Attendee rows with the same email for the same booking.
raw_findings.root_cause: The filter only checks against existing booking attendees and the blacklist, not against duplicate values within the submitted array itself.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Deduplicate `guests` (e.g. via `Array.from(new Set(guests))`) before filtering against existing attendees/blacklist, mirroring the uniqueness check already present client-side.
raw_findings.title: Guest list not deduplicated against itself before creating attendees
raw_findings.trigger: A caller (e.g. direct tRPC call bypassing the client-side Zod refine in AddGuestsDialog) submits a guests array containing the same new email address more than once (e.g. ["a@x.com","a@x.com"]).

raw_findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compares the un-lowercased submitted guest email against the lowercased blacklist, so the case-variant email is not recognized as blacklisted and is allowed through, bypassing the intended block.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Security/business control (email blacklist) can be bypassed via case variation.
raw_findings.impact: `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compares the un-lowercased submitted guest email against the lowercased blacklist, so the case-variant email is not recognized as blacklisted and is allowed through, bypassing the intended block.
raw_findings.root_cause: Only the blacklist array is normalized to lowercase; the compared guest value is left in its original case.
raw_findings.title: Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive against a lowercased blacklist
raw_findings.trigger: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS contains e.g. "blocked@example.com", and a user submits the guest email with different casing, e.g. "Blocked@Example.com".

raw_findings.body: The caught error object is discarded; only a generic string is logged, making it impossible to diagnose the actual cause of email delivery failures in production logs.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Loss of diagnostic information on failure, degrading observability/debuggability.
raw_findings.impact: The caught error object is discarded; only a generic string is logged, making it impossible to diagnose the actual cause of email delivery failures in production logs.
raw_findings.root_cause: The catch block ignores the bound `err` variable and logs only a static message.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Log the caught error, e.g. `console.error("Error sending AddGuestsEmails", err);` or use the shared logger with the error object.
raw_findings.title: Email send failure is logged without error details
raw_findings.trigger: sendAddGuestsEmails throws (e.g. SMTP failure, template error) while adding guests.

raw_findings.body: In sendAddGuestsEmails, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` uses the raw `guests` list (not the `uniqueGuests` list actually used to create new attendees), so a pre-existing attendee whose email happens to appear again in `guests` is misclassified as newly added and incorrectly receives the full 'scheduled' invite email (AttendeeScheduledEmail) instead of the 'guests added' notification (AttendeeAddGuestsEmail).
raw_findings.failure_mode: Existing attendees receive an incorrect email notification type on repeat/duplicate guest submissions.
raw_findings.impact: In sendAddGuestsEmails, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` uses the raw `guests` list (not the `uniqueGuests` list actually used to create new attendees), so a pre-existing attendee whose email happens to appear again in `guests` is misclassified as newly added and incorrectly receives the full 'scheduled' invite email (AttendeeScheduledEmail) instead of the 'guests added' notification (AttendeeAddGuestsEmail).
raw_findings.root_cause: The variable used for downstream email-type classification is not the same set that was actually inserted as new attendees.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass `uniqueGuests` (the actually-created new attendee emails) instead of the raw `guests` array to `sendAddGuestsEmails`.
raw_findings.title: Raw (unfiltered) guests array used to classify attendees for email templates
raw_findings.trigger: A caller resubmits the email of an already-existing attendee within the `guests` array (e.g. duplicate/typo re-add) together with genuinely new guest emails.

raw_findings.body: Unlike `sendLocationChangeEmails` in the same file, `sendAddGuestsEmails` unconditionally sends organizer and attendee emails, ignoring the event type's email-disable setting, resulting in unwanted notification emails being sent contrary to host configuration.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Email notifications sent even when the site/event configuration is intended to suppress them, causing unexpected communications.
raw_findings.impact: Unlike `sendLocationChangeEmails` in the same file, `sendAddGuestsEmails` unconditionally sends organizer and attendee emails, ignoring the event type's email-disable setting, resulting in unwanted notification emails being sent contrary to host configuration.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new function was implemented without the existing event-type-based email suppression convention already used by its sibling function in the same module.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Accept eventTypeMetadata (or a disable flag) in sendAddGuestsEmails and guard the attendee/organizer email pushes with `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(...)`/equivalent checks, consistent with `sendLocationChangeEmails`.
raw_findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails omits eventType-disable-email check used by sibling function
raw_findings.trigger: A booking's event type has attendee/organizer notification emails disabled (as respected elsewhere via `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`, see `sendLocationChangeEmails` in the same file), and a guest is added to that booking.

validated_findings.suggested_fix: Deduplicate `guests` (e.g. via `Array.from(new Set(guests))`) before filtering against existing attendees/blacklist, mirroring the uniqueness check already present client-side.
validated_findings.title: Guest list not deduplicated against itself before creating attendees
validated_findings.trigger: A caller (e.g. direct tRPC call bypassing the client-side Zod refine in AddGuestsDialog) submits a guests array containing the same new email address more than once (e.g. ["a@x.com","a@x.com"]).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 74-78 show uniqueGuests filters against existing attendees and blacklist, but does not deduplicate the input array itself. If guests=['a@x.com','a@x.com'] and neither exists, both pass filter and createMany inserts duplicates. Trigger requires bypassing client validation but is realistic for direct API calls.

validated_findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compares the un-lowercased submitted guest email against the lowercased blacklist, so the case-variant email is not recognized as blacklisted and is allowed through, bypassing the intended block.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Security/business control (email blacklist) can be bypassed via case variation.
validated_findings.impact: `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compares the un-lowercased submitted guest email against the lowercased blacklist, so the case-variant email is not recognized as blacklisted and is allowed through, bypassing the intended block.
validated_findings.root_cause: Only the blacklist array is normalized to lowercase; the compared guest value is left in its original case.
validated_findings.title: Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive against a lowercased blacklist
validated_findings.trigger: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS contains e.g. "blocked@example.com", and a user submits the guest email with different casing, e.g. "Blocked@Example.com".
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 70-77 show blacklist is lowercased but guest email in filter comparison (line 77) is not lowercased. `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compares raw guest against lowercased list, allowing case-variant bypass. This is a real case-sensitivity bug introduced by the patch.

validated_findings.body: The caught error object is discarded; only a generic string is logged, making it impossible to diagnose the actual cause of email delivery failures in production logs.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Loss of diagnostic information on failure, degrading observability/debuggability.
validated_findings.impact: The caught error object is discarded; only a generic string is logged, making it impossible to diagnose the actual cause of email delivery failures in production logs.
validated_findings.root_cause: The catch block ignores the bound `err` variable and logs only a static message.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Log the caught error, e.g. `console.error("Error sending AddGuestsEmails", err);` or use the shared logger with the error object.
validated_findings.title: Email send failure is logged without error details
validated_findings.trigger: sendAddGuestsEmails throws (e.g. SMTP failure, template error) while adding guests.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 167-171 show catch block logs static string 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails' but discards the `err` variable. This loses diagnostic information for debugging email failures. While low severity, it's a real observability issue introduced by the patch.

validated_findings.body: In sendAddGuestsEmails, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` uses the raw `guests` list (not the `uniqueGuests` list actually used to create new attendees), so a pre-existing attendee whose email happens to appear again in `guests` is misclassified as newly added and incorrectly receives the full 'scheduled' invite email (AttendeeScheduledEmail) instead of the 'guests added' notification (AttendeeAddGuestsEmail).
validated_findings.failure_mode: Existing attendees receive an incorrect email notification type on repeat/duplicate guest submissions.
validated_findings.impact: In sendAddGuestsEmails, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` uses the raw `guests` list (not the `uniqueGuests` list actually used to create new attendees), so a pre-existing attendee whose email happens to appear again in `guests` is misclassified as newly added and incorrectly receives the full 'scheduled' invite email (AttendeeScheduledEmail) instead of the 'guests added' notification (AttendeeAddGuestsEmail).
validated_findings.root_cause: The variable used for downstream email-type classification is not the same set that was actually inserted as new attendees.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Pass `uniqueGuests` (the actually-created new attendee emails) instead of the raw `guests` array to `sendAddGuestsEmails`.
validated_findings.title: Raw (unfiltered) guests array used to classify attendees for email templates
validated_findings.trigger: A caller resubmits the email of an already-existing attendee within the `guests` array (e.g. duplicate/typo re-add) together with genuinely new guest emails.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 168 passes raw `guests` array to sendAddGuestsEmails, not `uniqueGuests`. In email-manager.ts line 541, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` uses this to classify emails. If an existing attendee's email is resubmitted in guests array, they'd be misclassified as new and receive AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail.

validated_findings.body: Unlike `sendLocationChangeEmails` in the same file, `sendAddGuestsEmails` unconditionally sends organizer and attendee emails, ignoring the event type's email-disable setting, resulting in unwanted notification emails being sent contrary to host configuration.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Email notifications sent even when the site/event configuration is intended to suppress them, causing unexpected communications.
validated_findings.impact: Unlike `sendLocationChangeEmails` in the same file, `sendAddGuestsEmails` unconditionally sends organizer and attendee emails, ignoring the event type's email-disable setting, resulting in unwanted notification emails being sent contrary to host configuration.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new function was implemented without the existing event-type-based email suppression convention already used by its sibling function in the same module.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Accept eventTypeMetadata (or a disable flag) in sendAddGuestsEmails and guard the attendee/organizer email pushes with `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(...)`/equivalent checks, consistent with `sendLocationChangeEmails`.
validated_findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails omits eventType-disable-email check used by sibling function
validated_findings.trigger: A booking's event type has attendee/organizer notification emails disabled (as respected elsewhere via `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`, see `sendLocationChangeEmails` in the same file), and a guest is added to that booking.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 525-537 show sendAddGuestsEmails unconditionally sends emails without checking eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail, unlike sendLocationChangeEmails at lines 515-521 which does check. This inconsistency means email suppression settings are ignored for add-guests notifications.
